events.summary:
* WHAT...One to two feet of inundation above ground level in low-
lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Inland Sussex and Delaware Beaches.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM EST this evening.

* IMPACTS...At this level, widespread roadway flooding occurs
along tidal waterways. Some roads become impassable. Minor
damage to vulnerable structures may begin to occur. At this
level, flooding begins on the most vulnerable roads along
tidal waterways. Some partial or full road closures are
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Although no additional tidal flooding is
expected on the oceanfront and Delaware Bay, flooding will
linger on back bays including Rehoboth and Little Assawoman
Bays for the next several hours.

events.region: San Diego County Coastal Areas; Orange County Coastal
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Breaking surf of 4 to 7 feet with sets up to 8 feet on
exposed west-facing beaches and minor to locally moderate
coastal flooding.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...Through Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and beach
erosion. Large breaking waves can cause injury and wash people
off beaches and rocks. Low-lying parking lots and boardwalks
will flood during morning high tides.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides Saturday morning will be 7.0 to
7.1 feet and occur just after 11 AM PST.

events.summary:
* WHAT...Minor saltwater flooding.

* WHERE...Upper Florida Keys.

* WHEN...Through early Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Minor saltwater flooding of low elevation streets and
lots is likely. Some storm drains will overflow, and some
seawalls and docks will be overtopped. Boaters can expect less
clearance under fixed bridges. Motorists should remember that
persistent puddles around the times of high tide are almost
certain to contain a mix of saltwater.

events.region: Yukon Delta Coast; Lower Yukon River; Lower Yukon and Innoko Valleys
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Heavy snow and blowing snow possible. Total snow
accumulations of 3 to 7 inches possible. Wind gusts in the 45 to 60
mph range possible. Periods of blizzard conditions possible.

* WHERE...Lower Yukon River, Lower Yukon and Innoko Valleys, and
Yukon Delta Coast.

* WHEN...From Sunday evening through late Monday night.

* IMPACTS...Travel may be impacted. Periods of blowing and falling
snow could reduce visibilities to 1/4 mile or less at times.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Temperatures warm to near freezing throughout
the day Monday. Once near freezing, reduced visibility due to
blowing snow may improve. The strongest winds are expected near the
coast and valleys open to the east.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Bering Strait Coast; Southern Seward Peninsula Coast; Interior Seward Peninsula
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...For the Winter Weather Advisory snow and blowing snow
expected. Total snow accumulations between 2 and 4 inches. Winds
gusting up to 45 mph. For the Winter Storm Watch blowing snow
expected. Moderate snowfall expected. Wind gusts in the 45 to 60
mph range possible.

* WHERE...Bering Strait Coast, Interior Seward Peninsula, and
Southern Seward Peninsula Coast.

* WHEN...For the Winter Weather Advisory, from 3 PM this afternoon to
9 AM AKST Saturday. For the Winter Storm Watch, from Sunday evening
through Tuesday morning.

* IMPACTS...For the Winter Weather Advisory travel may be difficult.
Blowing and falling snow could reduce visibility to 1/2 mile or
less at times. For the Winter Storm Watch blizzard conditions
possible. Falling and blowing snow could reduce visibility to 1/4
mile or less at times.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...For the Winter Weather Advisory Winds peak
Friday night into Saturday morning and rapidly weaken by Saturday
afternoon. For the Winter Storm Watch winds peak Monday.
